lines.text: Add one, two, four, eight, and keep doubling. One hundred numbers!
lines.caption: Add one, two, four, eight, and keep doubling. One hundred numbers!

lines.text: The total is thirty-one digits long! Yet we can find its remainder.
lines.caption: The total is thirty-one digits long! Yet we can find its remainder.

lines.text: The last number is two to the ninety-ninth.
lines.caption: The last number is two to the ninety-ninth.

lines.text: What's the remainder when the sum is divided by seven?
lines.caption: What's the remainder when the sum is divided by seven?

lines.text: Here's the trick. Look at each number's remainder.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. Look at each number's remainder.

lines.text: One, two, four, then eight leaves one again. It's a cycle!
lines.caption: One, two, four, then eight leaves one again. It's a cycle!

lines.text: One plus two plus four is seven. Each group leaves nothing.
lines.caption: One plus two plus four is seven. Each group leaves nothing.

lines.text: Ninety-nine terms make thirty-three groups. The last term leaves one.
lines.caption: Ninety-nine terms make thirty-three groups. The last term leaves one.

lines.text: A giant sum, tamed by a tiny pattern.
lines.caption: A giant sum, tamed by a tiny pattern.

lines.text: Why a cycle? The full lesson shows two neat ways, plus every trap.
